summary: Tested eSign module end-to-end (backend + frontend). Created /app/backend/tests/test_esign_api.py with 17 pytest cases covering auth, CRUD, PDF magic-byte validation, multi-signer parallel signing flow (view → submit → completed → signed PDF download), invalid token handling, verify endpoint with masked emails, void, and delete. ALL 17 BACKEND TESTS PASS. Frontend tested: landing, tools-hub card, dashboard (anon redirect + auth list with status filters), wizard (5 steps), public signing route, public verify route. All major flows functional; 2 minor UX polish issues found.

ui_bugs.issue: When document not found, the page renders a friendly 'Document not found' heading BUT also shows the raw JSON body '{"detail":"Document not found"}' below it. This raw error envelope leaks to end users on a public route and looks unpolished.

Invalid token renders 'Unable to open document' followed by the raw error code string 'AUTH_REQUIRED'. End users will be confused by the technical token. Suggest mapping AUTH_REQUIRED -> friendlier sentence (e.g., 'This signing link is invalid or has been revoked. Please contact the sender.').

issues: Page is accessible without authentication — anonymous users can view step 1 (Upload). This is likely intentional since the upload API call is the auth gate, but consider an early redirect-to-login for UX clarity if not desired.

action_items: (Optional UX) On /verify/[docId], suppress raw JSON body when showing 'Document not found' — keep only the friendly heading.
(Optional UX) On /sign/[token] invalid-token state, replace raw 'AUTH_REQUIRED' string with a user-friendly explanation.
critical_code_review_comments: routes.py line 151 uses __import__('sqlalchemy').Integer inside a func.cast — this works but is unidiomatic; import sqlalchemy.Integer at top of module for readability.

routes.py uses transient attribute 's.__send_token' on ORM objects to pass raw tokens to background tasks. Works but is fragile (SQLAlchemy may complain on refresh); consider returning a list of (signer, token) tuples instead.

routes.py /sign/{token}/submit catches `signer.token_used` after _resolve_token but a completed document still allows _resolve_token to succeed (no 410 on status=='completed'). Currently 'Already signed' (403) is raised via token_used flag — works, but adding an explicit 410 when doc.status=='completed' would be cleaner.
schemas.py SignerOut.email is plain `str` but the model stores lowercased email — fine, but expose the verified shape.
Email service uses Resend onboarding@resend.dev sender — clearly noted as mocked-delivery; production will need a verified domain sender.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all routes load and work; 2 minor UX polish items)

seed_data_creation: Tests auto-create 'TEST_'-prefixed documents and delete them in teardown. Note: one previously created 'E2E Test Contract' (Completed, by main agent) and one 'Test Contract' (Draft) are persisted in PostgreSQL from prior manual testing — left intact.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is solid. The signing-completion logic correctly transitions status to 'completed', populates signed_key, recomputes doc_hash, and the signed PDF downloads as %PDF-1.x. Sequential signing branch is NOT yet covered by automated tests (only parallel) — if regression-testing, add a sequential test by setting signing_order='sequential' on PATCH and verifying only the first signer's token is initially active. The PDF.js worker loads from cdnjs CDN; if the wizard step 3 (Place Fields) needs deeper testing, requires uploading a real PDF and waiting for canvas render (~3-5s). PostgreSQL tables: documents, signers, signature_fields, audit_events — inspect via `su - postgres -c "psql -d realprofits_esign -c '\dt'"`.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. The two reported UI polish items are cosmetic: error states show raw API envelope/code strings to public users on /verify and /sign error paths; recommend mapping to friendlier copy in the respective Next.js pages.
